label: NO2
definition: How much nitrogen dioxide, a gas released mainly by burning fuel, sits in the lower atmosphere (tropospheric air column) above the area, measured by the Aura satellite.
reading_hint: Higher usually means more combustion (traffic, power, industry, fires), but weather and sunlight also change how fast it disperses or breaks down.

label: Wind speed
definition: How fast the wind blows 10 metres above the ground.
reading_hint: Stronger wind spreads pollution out and increases drying; calm air lets pollution build up.

label: Cloud amount
definition: The share of the sky covered by cloud.
reading_hint: Clouds also block the satellite's view, so this helps judge how much to trust NO₂ months.

label: Pressure
definition: The air pressure at the ground surface.
reading_hint: Changes over time track high-pressure fair weather versus low-pressure storms; average levels also depend on ground elevation.

label: Clear-sky sunlight
definition: The sunlight energy that would reach the ground if the sky were cloud-free.
reading_hint: Mainly set by the season and latitude (plus atmospheric haze and water vapour); it is the cloudless ceiling.

label: Cloud sunlight reduction
definition: How much sunlight power clouds blocked before reaching the ground: clear-sky minus actual sunlight, converted to watts per square metre.
reading_hint: Larger means cloudier skies took away more sun.

label: Vegetation fire density
definition: How many satellite-detected heat spots from presumed vegetation fires appear per 1,000 km² per day observed by the satellite (nominal and high confidence).
reading_hint: Counts detected pixels across satellite overpasses, not distinct fires or burned area; higher means more detected burning from wildfires, farm burning or war-related fires.

label: Static heat sources
definition: Persistent stationary heat spots on land that are not vegetation fires, such as steelworks, industrial plants and gas flares, per 1,000 km² per satellite-observed day.
reading_hint: A steady industrial background reading; sharp drops or rises usually mean plants or flares stopped, started or were damaged.

label: Air temperature
definition: The monthly average air temperature 2 metres above the ground.
reading_hint: The basic measure of warm or cold.

label: Peak temperature
definition: The single hottest air temperature reached 2 metres above the ground at any time during the month (monthly extreme peak, not an average of daily highs).
reading_hint: Captures monthly heat extremes, which spike wildfire and heat-stress risk.

label: Temperature range
definition: The daily gap between daytime high and nighttime low air temperature, averaged over the month.
reading_hint: A wider average daily swing points to clear, dry days and cooler nights; a narrow gap points to cloudy or humid air.

label: All-sky sunlight
definition: The sunlight energy actually reaching the ground each day, with clouds included.
reading_hint: Less than clear-sky sunlight whenever it is cloudy; drives surface heating and evaporation.

label: Evaporation demand (PET)
definition: How much water the air and sun could pull in a day from a hypothetical well-watered reference grass field (the FAO-56 standard benchmark).
reading_hint: Higher means thirstier air and potential faster drying of soil and crops; actual evaporation is lower when soils are dry.

label: Rainfall
definition: The total rain and melted snowfall reaching the ground, as millimetres of liquid water per day (bias-corrected reanalysis).
reading_hint: The main supply of water to land.

label: VPD (drying demand)
definition: How dry the air feels to plants: the gap between saturation vapour pressure at that temperature and the air's actual vapour pressure.
reading_hint: Higher means the air pulls moisture out of leaves and damp soil faster.

label: Specific humidity
definition: The mass of water vapour mixed into the air, in grams per kilogram of moist air at 2 metres height.
reading_hint: Higher means the air actually carries more moisture, independent of temperature.

label: Relative humidity
definition: How close the air's water vapour is to saturation, as a percentage of the maximum it could hold at that temperature.
reading_hint: Lower values mean drier air, either because moisture fell or because temperature rose.

label: Transpiration
definition: Model-estimated water that plants release into the air through their leaves each day (MERRA-2 canopy transpiration, converted from energy flux).
reading_hint: Drops near zero in dormant winter; higher in warm months means active, growing vegetation with available root water.

label: Water balance (P - PET)
definition: Total precipitation (rain and melted snow) minus reference evaporation demand (PET): the climatic water surplus or deficit.
reading_hint: Below zero (common in summer) means atmospheric demand exceeds water supplied by precipitation.

label: Surface soil wetness
definition: Reanalysis model estimate of how wet the top 5 cm of soil is, from 0 (completely water-free) to 1 (saturated).
reading_hint: Reacts quickly to recent rain and dry spells.

label: Root-zone wetness
definition: Reanalysis model estimate of how wet the soil is down to 1 metre, where most roots grow, from 0 (completely water-free) to 1 (saturated).
reading_hint: Shows whether crops and vegetation have moisture in reserve.

label: Full-profile wetness
definition: Reanalysis model estimate of wetness across the entire soil column from the surface to bedrock, from 0 (completely water-free) to 1 (saturated).
reading_hint: Changes slowly; tracks multi-season dry or wet periods.

label: Surface temperature
definition: The modelled radiative skin temperature of the ground surface itself, rather than the air 2 metres above it.
reading_hint: Rises with strong sun and dry ground.

label: Surface-air diff
definition: How much warmer or cooler the modelled ground skin surface is than the air 2 metres above it, as a 24-hour monthly mean.
reading_hint: Across 24-hour monthly averages, values stay near zero (-1.4 to +2.0 °C); positive summer shifts point to stronger heating or drier ground, while winter values often turn negative under snow or radiative cooling.

label: Albedo
definition: The share of incoming sunlight the ground reflects back upward, from 0 (none) to 1 (all).
reading_hint: Snow and bright bare soil reflect more; dark forest and green or wet fields reflect less.
